subject.title: iPhone Continuity Camera `--facing front` always uses rear camera

question: For macOS camera capture, should an explicit `deviceId` remain the highest-precedence selector when `facing` is also provided for an iPhone Continuity Camera?
rationale: Current code treats `deviceId` as an exact camera selector, while this report expects `facing` to select a lens within the Continuity Camera device; that contract needs maintainer intent and live AVFoundation proof.

options.title: Preserve exact device targeting
options.body: Run live Continuity proof first; if macOS exposes no supported front/back lens selector for that device id, document or return a clear limitation while keeping `deviceId` exact.

options.title: Support Continuity lens remapping
options.body: If live proof shows a supported selector for the same iPhone device, add a narrow macOS implementation with tests and docs.

options.title: Let facing override device id
options.body: Change selector precedence so `facing` can replace an explicit device id, accepting compatibility risk for existing multi-camera workflows.

recommendation.title: Preserve exact device targeting
recommendation.body: Run live Continuity proof first; if macOS exposes no supported front/back lens selector for that device id, document or return a clear limitation while keeping `deviceId` exact.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest observed history across the macOS camera service and camera CLI refactors tied to this behavior.
